answer: Scarcity Ledger. Each identity must submit a fresh, physically unique sensor trace of a landmark's ledge geometry captured at a registered site, hashed against a public basalt formation survey that no operator can fabricate without field access. The rule ties issuance to that karst-mapped coordinate set, so impersonation requires physically visiting and surveying each distinct site. An attacker pays travel and survey time per identity, roughly a full day per credential, and duplicate coordinates are rejected outright.
